name: Amaziah the priest of Bethel
charge: Forbidding Amos to prophesy at the king's chapel; accusing him to Jeroboam of conspiracy
summary: A priest of the calf at Bethel sent word to Jeroboam that Amos had conspired against him, then told the prophet to go earn his bread in Judah. Amos answered that he was no prophet's son but a herdman the Lord had taken from the flock, and gave Amaziah a sentence for his wife, his children, his land and himself.
offense: Amos had pleaded for Jacob when shown judgments of grasshoppers and fire. The Lord then showed him a plumbline set in the midst of Israel and declared the coming desolation of its high places and sanctuaries (Amos 7:1-9). The prophet who announced judgment had first interceded for the people; rebuke was not proof that he wished their destruction. Amaziah sent word to Jeroboam that Amos had conspired against him and that the land could not bear his words. He then told Amos to flee to Judah, eat bread there, and prophesy no more at Bethel because it was the king's chapel and court (Amos 7:10-13). The priest treated the royal sanctuary as a place where the king's interests could set the limits of the Lord's speech. Amos answered that he had been a herdman and a gatherer of sycamore fruit. The Lord had taken him from following the flock and sent him to prophesy to Israel (Amos 7:14-15). His commission was not employment that Amaziah could transfer to another country. The question was not where he might earn bread, but to whom the Lord had sent him.
judgment: Amos turned Amaziah's prohibition back upon him: because he said not to prophesy against Israel, a word now came concerning his own house. His wife would be a harlot in the city, his sons and daughters would fall by the sword, his land would be divided, and he would die in a polluted land. Israel would surely go into captivity (Amos 7:16-17). The sentence reached the things his royal protection could not secure: household, children, inheritance, and burial land. Silence imposed upon the messenger would not silence the judgment or preserve the place from which he was expelled. The king named here was Jeroboam in the days of Amos, not Jeroboam son of Nebat who first established the calves. Generations had passed, yet Bethel's service still joined royal power to resistance against the Lord's word. The priest defended the sanctuary's standing while refusing the correction that exposed its condition.

verses.text: Then Amaziah the priest of Beth–el sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, Amos hath conspired against thee in the midst of the house of Israel: the land is not able to bear all his words.
For thus Amos saith, Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall surely be led away captive out of their own land.
Also Amaziah said unto Amos, O thou seer, go, flee thee away into the land of Judah, and there eat bread, and prophesy there:
But prophesy not again any more at Beth–el: for it is the king’s chapel, and it is the king’s court.
Then answered Amos, and said to Amaziah, I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet’s son; but I was an herdman, and a gatherer of sycomore fruit:
And the Lord took me as I followed the flock, and the Lord said unto me, Go, prophesy unto my people Israel.
Now therefore hear thou the word of the Lord: Thou sayest, Prophesy not against Israel, and drop not thy word against the house of Isaac.

Therefore thus saith the Lord; Thy wife shall be an harlot in the city, and thy sons and thy daughters shall fall by the sword, and thy land shall be divided by line; and thou shalt die in a polluted land: and Israel shall surely go into captivity forth of his land.
And I raised up of your sons for prophets, and of your young men for Nazarites. Is it not even thus, O ye children of Israel? saith the Lord.
But ye gave the Nazarites wine to drink; and commanded the prophets, saying, Prophesy not.
And he made an house of high places, and made priests of the lowest of the people, which were not of the sons of Levi.

And Jeroboam ordained a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like unto the feast that is in Judah, and he offered upon the altar. So did he in Beth–el, sacrificing unto the calves that he had made: and he placed in Beth–el the priests of the high places which he had made.

So he offered upon the altar which he had made in Beth–el the fifteenth day of the eighth month, even in the month which he had devised of his own heart; and ordained a feast unto the children of Israel: and he offered upon the altar, and burnt incense.
And the Lord God of their fathers sent to them by his messengers, rising up betimes, and sending; because he had compassion on his people, and on his dwelling place:
But they mocked the messengers of God, and despised his words, and misused his prophets, until the wrath of the Lord arose against his people, till there was no remedy.

entries.commentary: The Most High showed Amos grasshoppers formed in the beginning of the shooting up of the latter growth, after the king's mowings, and they ate the grass of the land. Amos pleaded, asking by whom shall Jacob arise, for he is small, and the Lord repented and said it shall not be.

The Most High showed Amos that he called to contend by fire, and it devoured the great deep and ate up a part. Amos again beseeched him to cease, asking by whom shall Jacob arise, for he is small, and the Lord repented and said this also shall not be.

The Lord stood upon a wall made by a plumbline with a plumbline in his hand and asked Amos what he saw, and Amos said a plumbline. The Most High will set a plumbline in the midst of his people Israel and will not again pass by them anymore. The high places of Isaac shall be desolate, the sanctuaries of Israel laid waste, and he will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.

Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent word to Jeroboam that Amos had conspired against him and that the land could not bear his words. Amaziah told Amos to flee into the land of Judah, eat bread there, and prophesy no more at Bethel, for it was the king's chapel and court.

Amos answered that he was no prophet nor a prophet's son, but a herdman and a gatherer of sycamore fruit whom the Lord took as he followed the flock and sent to prophesy unto his people Israel. Because Amaziah said prophesy not against Israel, the Most High declared his wife would be a harlot in the city, his sons and daughters fall by the sword, his land divided, and he would die in a polluted land while Israel goes into captivity. Amaziah was trying to get the brother to stop prophesying, and judgment came upon him for that. The Most High gives his word to the prophets, and the prophet's job is to carry out the word of the Lord, no more, no less. If you do not like it, too bad.

For three transgressions of Moab and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because he burned the bones of the king of Edom into lime. Moab today is the Chinese. He will send a fire upon Moab that shall devour the palaces of Kerioth, and Moab shall die with tumult, with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet, and he will cut off the judge and slay all the princes with him.

For three transgressions of Judah and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they despised the law of the Lord, did not keep his commandments, and their lies caused them to err after which their fathers walked. This is the reason we are in captivity even today. Going back to the Assyrian captivity, our forefathers were rebellious against the Most High's laws, did not want to keep the commandments, and wanted to worship idols. He will send a fire upon Judah that shall devour the palaces of Jerusalem.

For three transgressions of Israel and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they sold the righteous for silver and the poor for a pair of shoes. That goes into oppression, and just like in today's time nobody wants to hear the righteous words of the Most High and keep the commandments; when you bring out the commandments you hear "what, I can't wear pants." They pant after the dust of the earth on the head of the poor, turn aside the way of the meek, and a man and his father go in unto the same maid to profane the Most High's holy name. There were men even in that time going in unto their father's wife, and you may find a TV show today promoting that behavior. They lay themselves down upon clothes laid to pledge by every altar and drink the wine of the condemned in the house of their god. -

Yet the Most High destroyed the Amorite before them, whose height was like the height of the cedar and who was strong as the oaks; he destroyed his fruit from above and his roots from beneath. The Amorite is another heathen nation. He brought Israel up from the land of Egypt, led them forty years through the wilderness to possess the land of the Amorite, and raised up their sons for prophets and their young men for Nazirites. You can use this to show that the children of Israel are the prophets of the Most High. But they gave the Nazirites wine to drink and commanded the prophets saying, prophesy not. That goes into lies and deceit, doing anything to stop the word of the Most High.

The Most High is pressed under them as a cart is pressed that is full of sheaves; therefore the flight shall perish from the swift, the strong shall not strengthen his force, and the mighty shall not deliver himself, because Israel will be in captivity. He that is courageous among the mighty shall flee away naked in that day; every possession you had will be stripped from you as you flee, the same way a robber coming to a bank strips everybody down and takes the goods.

Rehoboam went to Shechem, where all Israel came to make him king. Jeroboam, still in Egypt, heard of it and returned, and the congregation of Israel came to Rehoboam asking him to lighten the grievous yoke and heavy service his father had put on them. The heavy yoke was the labor of the building; Solomon did not enslave his own people as he did the other nations, but they did have to put in that work. Rehoboam told them to depart three days and return, which was wisdom, for it is right to take time and get counsel before giving an answer.

Rehoboam consulted the old men that stood before Solomon his father, who advised that if he would be a servant to the people and speak good words, they would be his servants forever, but he forsook their counsel and consulted the young men he grew up with. Solomon was the wisest man on earth and still had counselors, yet Rehoboam forsook the counselors of the wisest man for his peers. The problem is getting counsel from those on your own level rather than from elders. The young men told him to say his little finger would be thicker than his father's loins, and that where his father chastised them with whips he would chastise them with scorpions, which was disrespectful.

When Jeroboam and the people came the third day, Rehoboam answered roughly, forsaking the old men's counsel, and told them he would add to their yoke and chastise them with scorpions. The king hearkened not to the people, for the cause was from the Most High, that he might perform the saying he spoke by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam; the prophecy had to come to pass.

When all Israel saw the king would not hearken, they said, What portion have we in David? To your tents, O Israel. So Israel departed and rebelled against the house of David to this day, and only over those in the cities of Judah did Rehoboam reign. Rehoboam sent Adoram who was over the tribute, and all Israel stoned him with stones, so the king fled in his chariot to Jerusalem. This is the split, the northern tribes rebelling against the house of David until this day. When Israel heard Jeroboam had returned, they called him to the congregation and made him king over Israel; none followed the house of David but the tribe of Judah only. That is how Jeroboam got the ten tribes.

Rehoboam assembled the house of Judah with Benjamin, a hundred and eighty thousand chosen warriors, to fight against the house of Israel and bring the kingdom back to himself. But the word of the Most High came to Shemaiah the man of God, telling Rehoboam and the house of Judah and Benjamin not to fight against their brethren the children of Israel, for this thing was from the Most High; and they hearkened and returned home.

Jeroboam built Shechem in mount Ephraim and Penuel, and feared in his heart that if the people went up to sacrifice at Jerusalem their hearts would turn again to Rehoboam king of Judah and they would kill him. Jeroboam took counsel and made two calves of gold, telling Israel it was too much to go up to Jerusalem, and setting one calf in Bethel and the other in Dan, and this thing became a sin. He made a house of high places and priests of the lowest of the people, not of the sons of Levi. Jeroboam ordained a feast in the eighth month on the fifteenth day, a feast he devised of his own heart, and offered on the altar at Bethel sacrificing to the calves he made. Devising your own holy days and throwing off the days of the Most High is the same error men make today, and after forty years of peace under Solomon the nation of Israel began to decline even more.

The people of the land take Jehoahaz the son of Josiah and make him king in Jerusalem; he is twenty three years old and reigns three months. The king of Egypt puts him down, condemns the land in a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold, and makes Eliakim his brother king, turning his name to Jehoiakim, and carries Jehoahaz to Egypt.

Jehoiakim is twenty five years old when he begins to reign and reigns eleven years in Jerusalem, doing evil in the sight of the Lord his God, so Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon comes up against him and binds him in fetters to carry him to Babylon. Nebuchadnezzar also carries off the vessels of the house of the Lord to Babylon and puts them in his temple. The Most High set a wicked king over the land because his own people would not do what he said. The power of the earth is in the hand of the Most High, and in due time he sets over it one that is profitable. When Israel will not rule in righteousness, he raises a Nebuchadnezzar; Israel's purpose was never to be wicked and rule at the same time. -

Jehoiachin is eight years old when he begins to reign and reigns three months and ten days in Jerusalem, and he does that which is evil in the sight of the Lord. When the year is expired, Nebuchadnezzar sends and brings him to Babylon with the goodly vessels of the house of the Lord, and makes Zedekiah his brother king over Judah.

Zedekiah is twenty one years old when he begins to reign and reigns eleven years, and he does evil in the sight of the Lord his God and humbles not himself before Jeremiah the prophet speaking from the mouth of the Lord. He rebels against Nebuchadnezzar who had made him swear by God, and stiffens his neck and hardens his heart from turning to the Lord God of Israel. The chief priests and people transgress very much after all the abominations of the heathen and pollute the house of the Lord. The Most High sends to them by his messengers, rising up early and sending because he had compassion, but they mock the messengers, despise his words, and misuse his prophets until the wrath of the Lord arises and there is no remedy. -

The Most High brings upon them the king of the Chaldees, who slays their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary and has no compassion upon young man or maiden, old man or him that stooped for age. He gives them all into Nebuchadnezzar's hand, and all the vessels of the house of God, great and small, and the treasures of the house of the Lord and of the king and his princes are brought to Babylon. They burn the house of God, break down the walls of Jerusalem, burn its palaces, and destroy all the goodly vessels, exactly the fierce nation the curses warned of. -

Those who escape the sword are carried away to Babylon, where they are servants to Nebuchadnezzar and his sons until the reign of the kingdom of Persia. This fulfills the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah, that the land would enjoy her sabbaths and lie desolate to fulfill threescore and ten years.

In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the Lord by Jeremiah might be accomplished, the Most High stirs up the spirit of Cyrus to make a proclamation throughout all his kingdom. Cyrus declares that the Lord God of heaven has given him all the kingdoms of the earth and charged him to build him a house in Jerusalem, and calls any of the Lord's people to go up, showing again that the Most High sets over the earth one that is profitable for his purpose. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)
